housing: Rossendale's towns fill the narrow Pennine valleys, and most of the housing is Victorian stone terraces built for the cotton and slipper mills, many on steep hillsides. Bacup and Stacksteads have some of the cheapest homes and a sizeable private rented sector, while Rawtenstall, Haslingden and Helmshore mix terraces with post-war and newer estates. Some mills have been converted to flats. Damp and exposure to Pennine weather are common issues in the older stone homes.
checkinTips: Stone terraces in Bacup and Stacksteads: photograph damp at the base of walls, cellars, and mould in back rooms built into the hillside.
Hillside homes throughout the valley: record steps, retaining walls, gutters and downpipes and any water coming off the slope.
Terraces near the River Irwell in Stacksteads and Waterfoot: photograph any tide marks, damp low on walls and air bricks.
Mill conversions: note fob and key counts, intercom, parking and the state of shared corridors.
Older homes with gas fires or stoves: photograph the appliances, chimneys and carbon monoxide alarms.
tenantHelp: Tenants can report disrepair, damp or unsafe conditions in privately rented homes to Rossendale Borough Council's environmental health team.
